claims.nibble_order: lower logical K index is the low nibble; next K index is the high nibble
claims.weight_scale_application: multiply decoded FP4 value by the stored scale

literal_case.derivation: 0x21 -> low code 1 (0.5), high code 2 (1.0); official kernel multiplies by E8M0 scale 0x80 (=2.0)

source_evidence: convert.py casts packed int8 bytes to uint8, extracts low=x&0x0F and high=(x>>4)&0x0F, then stacks [low, high] along K
kernel.py fp4_gemm uses one weight scale per 32 K values and multiplies GEMM partials by activation_scale * weight_scale
model.py allocates FP4 weights as [out, in//2] and FP4 scales as [out, in//32] in float8_e8m0fnu
convert.py renames weight_scale_inv to scale without reciprocating it
